title: Usage paths and migration lane for tokens, actions, tables, charts
creator: Riley Chen
description: Purpose: produce a compact, searchable set of usage paths and a step-by-step migration lane for teams updating product UI from legacy tokens and component variants to the new design system semantics. Scope covers: token naming and theming migration, action/button variants and usage dos/don’ts, data table ergonomics (sorting, density, selection), and chart color/accessibility guidelines. Deliverables: concise migration guide, code snippets and codemod examples, canonical example pages for each component, and a checklist for Product/Platform engineers to sign-off on changes.
acceptance_criteria: One central migration lane doc that maps legacy token names to new semantic tokens with code snippets for CSS/JS/Swift/Kotlin
Button section includes clear primary/secondary/ghost usage rules, dos/don’ts screenshots, and 3 real-world examples from Redwood’s console
Tables guidance covers density, keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, and a recommended default configuration for Dedicated customers
Chart guidance includes color-contrast primitives, recommended palettes for color-blindness, and a short reactive example for accessibility labels
A runnable example folder (links to sandbox) with live snippets for tokens, a button matrix, a data table with pagination+selection, and an annotated chart
PR with docs + example code approved by Eng and PM, and a short rollout checklist for migration (owners, release gating, telemetry to watch)
Migration codemod examples for common token rename patterns and at least one sample CI job to run linting for deprecated token usage

notes: Design goal is to reduce developer friction when migrating while preventing UX regressions. Keep docs compact (one page per component type plus a single migration lane) to increase consumption. Use telemetry (deprecated-token-usage metric) during rollout to know when customers have migrated.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Token mapping CSV + codemod POC (owner: Eng). Phase 2: Component example pages (buttons, tables, charts) with screenshots and annotated do/don’ts (owner: Design). Phase 3: Integrate examples into docs site, add CI lint rule, and ship release ds-docs-2026.04. Each phase ends with a cross-team review and sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams may not have bandwidth to run codemods immediately. Mitigation: provide manual migration checklist and a low-risk opt-in approach per repo.
Risk: Visual regressions in critical flows (billing, sign-in) when tokens switch. Mitigation: add a canary rollout plan and visual diff job for key routes.
Risk: Accessibility gaps in charts if palettes are misapplied. Mitigation: require an accessibility sign-off and include palette validators in examples.
